title: LIONS PIN DOWN HISTORY
author: Bill Haufe
content:
LIONS PIN DOWN HISTORY

 January 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 981
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — John Waters, Queen Anne's County High's girls head wrestling coach, wondered if his team recognized it was wrestling with history.Then again, maybe Queen Anne's was more focused on just winning than getting its name in the record books.
The Lions got both Friday night, stringing together five consecutive pinfalls before Kaylynn Bryant delivered a first-period fall in the second-to-last match that clinched Queen Anne's 48-36 victory over Winters Mill in the first girls dual match in the history of the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association, where all 14 weight classes competed without a forfeit.
"I don't think they realized the magnitude of the match; that Winters Mill was one of the first true girls teams," Waters said of his team. "They don't forfeit weight classes."
On this night, neither did Queen Anne's.
"They come in every day; they work," Waters said of his team. "And it's just like, 'OK, cool. It's time to wrestle.' I'm extremely proud of them."
Winters Mill defeated Queen Anne's a year ago in a dual meet in Centreville. The two met again in the finals of Maverick Duals at Manchester Valley in December, with Queen Anne's earning a 48-36 victory — the same score as Friday — ending the Falcons' two-year win streak.
Friday's third clash had the early markings of another close finish.
Queen Anne's Annalise Michael — one of seven first-year wrestlers in the Lions' starting lineup Friday — rallied from a 12-5 deficit to pin Nijae Tate in 4:21 of the 100-pound match.
"Started out with Annalise; that was a big swing match that we won," Waters said. "She fought off her back a couple of times and ended up getting the pin. I think that provided a lot of energy for the girls and they fed off it."
Winters Mill tied the match 6-all at 105, Alexa Hresko earning a first-period fall over Celeste Molina. Queen Anne's needed just 1:19 to move back in front, when Ally Conley, who won a state title in 2022, caught Carli Ireland in a headlock and hit a throw for a fall at 110. The Falcons again answered, as Christina Padilla (115) pinned Bevyn Branham in 1:03.
The Lions then reeled off five consecutive pins to build a commanding 30-point cushion.
Bree Conard — granddaughter of Hall of Fame coach Dan Zottarelli, who guided Kent County High's boys to back-to-back 2A-1A state titles in 2001-02, and was in attendance Friday — was taken down in the first period, but worked off bottom to register a fall in 2:28 over Jayla Shropshire at 120, giving the Lions a lead they never relinquished at 18-12.
Finley Patchett (125), another first-year wrestler, rolled Taylor Scholl to her back for a pin in 1:22. Queen Anne's Delaney Gray followed suit at 130, pinning Hailee Smith in 1:21 for a 30-12 lead. Linda Vail continued the roll, with a fall over Maggie Morley in 3:38 of the 135-pound match. Winters Mill's Kayla Goodwin (140) looked ready to end that streak, when she built a 4-1 lead on Keira Corcoran in the first period. But Corcoran scored an early reverse in the second en route to pinning Goodwin in 3:22.
"Tonight we got the matchups that we wanted and they were better," said Winters Mill head coach John Lowe, a St. Michaels High graduate who coached Waters at McDaniel College from 1997-99. "All props to coach Waters. He does a great job."
But Waters, who won a state title at 103 pounds for Queen Anne's in 1996, deflected any credit afterwards.
"I'm happy for all the girls," Waters said. "I'm extremely happy for (boys head) coach (Dave) Stricker. I just sat in the corner. If it wasn't for coach Stricker and his vision a couple of years ago, we wouldn't have the girls team.
"It just so happened that he's coaching one team and we needed a coach for the other team," Waters continued. "This is a team effort. I'm just one of the coaches. We have several coaches that are at practice every day that help these girls, and boys, wrestle. It's great for the program."
Winters Mill ended the Lions' run at 145, when Kimora Harrid pinned Lilly Hammond in the first period, and began whittling away at its deficit. The Falcons' Gabbie McLeod followed with a first-period fall over Morgan Morris at 155. Maiah Sweet (165) moved Winters Mill within 42-30 with a first-period pin of Addie Dickens.
The Falcons had a chance to draw even with two matches remaining, but those hopes ended when Bryant pinned Morgan Tolle with 7 seconds remaining in the first period of the 190-pound match, pushing the Lions' lead to 48-30.
"We had a couple of girls, they got their first varsity matches tonight and stepped in for some girls that were injured, and some that were sick," Waters said. "To not have our true lineup and to come in and do what we did. … Pretty impressive. I give all the credit to the girls."
Winters Mill's Jade Love (235) capped the match with a first-period pin of Maggie Rooney.
"They won it tonight. But we're going to focus on March now," Lowe said in reference to this year's state tournament, where a girls' team champion will be crowned for the first time in MPSSAA history. "We've got some stuff to work on before March."
Stricker, who watched his boys team defeat Winters Mill, 42-34, before losing to Southern of Anne Arundel, 42-33, snuck a couple glances at the girls match between the two boys dual bouts.
"We're probably the two biggest teams in the state of Maryland," Stricker said of Queen Anne's and Winters Mill, who figure to get competition from Francis Scott Key, La Plata and Manchester Valley at the state tournament. "To go toe-to-toe three times (with Winters Mill), it's what you want to grow the sport. They're exciting matches. Hope we can convince somebody up top that we can have a girls state duals at some point."

author: Bill Haufe

STEP BY STEP

 January 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 763
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — James Gardner's instructions to freshman Matthew Brunner were simple."The last thing I told him before he got out on the mat: Wrestle hard. Stay aggressive. And stay off your back," Easton High's head wrestling coach said.
Brunner checked all those boxes in what was perhaps the biggest match of his young career, pinning St. Michaels' Oliver Cummings midway through the first period of Friday's final bout to seal a 39-30 victory that extended the Warriors' win streak to three.
"That's exactly what we needed," Gardner said of Brunner's fall which helped raise Easton's record to 3-8 overall and in the Bayside Conference. "I'm really happy with his outcome and his progression."
St. Michaels (0-7, 0-7) never trailed until the ninth match, when Easton's Hayden Allen won by forfeit at 157 pounds, nudging the Warriors to a 21-18 lead. The Saints regained the lead at 24-21 in the next match, as Blake Foy built a 4-0 first-period advantage before pinning Kameron Popal in 3:34 of the 165-pound bout.
But the Warriors won the three of the remaining four bouts, starting with senior Matt Svehla's 15-second fall over Andrew Moorehead at 175.
"He's been one of my most consistent wrestlers this year," Gardner said of Svehla, who has yet to lose a conference match this season. "He's still working, still trying to get better on a daily basis.
"Tonight he just knew what he needed to get done," Gardner added of Svehla. "He knew we needed more than a win. We needed a pin because I tell them every point matters. I just appreciate him as a young man and a wrestler. I wish I had him for another year."
Svehla's pin moved Easton into the lead at 27-24. Liam Lewis widened that margin to 33-24 in a swing match, when he pinned Max Reed in 1:23 at 190.
"We definitely needed the match with Liam Lewis," Gardner said. "He's normally at 170, but we pushed him up to 190. That was big."
Will Bridges picked up a forfeit at 215, drawing St. Michaels within 33-30, and giving the Saints a chance to either tie or win heading into the final match at 285.
But Brunner followed Gardner's instructions, getting a takedown of Cummings before turning his opponent to his back for a fall with 1:02 remaining in the first period.
"I knew I just had to go out there and do my job to get the win," Brunner said. "At first I wasn't thinking I was going to get a pin. But I went in there confident and ended up getting the pin.
"It feels amazing," said Brunner, who after having his arm raised in victory received a big smile and handshake from Gardner before getting surrounded by his celebrating teammates. "When it's down to you and you go out there and get a win, it's a big one."
St. Michaels took a 6-0 lead in the opening match, as Will Coale led 4-0 after one period, watched his lead get trimmed to 4-2 by John Seymour 40 seconds into the second before earning a reversal and notching a fall with 3 seconds left in the second period at 106.
Easton cut that deficit in half via Gabe Trise's 14-8 decision over Hudson Jones at 113. St. Michaels' Andrew Sanchez (120) answered with a 6-1 win over Jakob Barnhart, restoring the Saints' six-point cushion.
Then came four consecutive forfeits. Easton's Shawn Arnold won a forfeit at 126 to make it 9-9. St. Michaels' Jacob Jenkins took a forfeit at 132, pushing the Saints back to a 15-9 lead. After a double forfeit at 138, Easton's Adonis Schmitt won by forfeit at 144, leaving the match even at 15-all.
St. Michaels' took its final lead at 150. After a scoreless first, Easton's Teddy Antal hit a reversal for a 2-0 lead. But St. Michaels' Lane Cappa took over from there. Despite two blood stoppages, Cappa rallied for a 4-2 lead, watched Antal escape, then scored three near-fall points for a 7-3 lead. Antal closed with a takedown with 28 seconds remaining in the match, but couldn't get any closer, as Cappa hit a switch for a 9-5 final and an 18-15 Saints lead.
"We're trying to get there," said St. Michaels' first-year head coach Steve Mister, one of the most outstanding wrestlers to ever come through the Saints' program. "We're going through growing pains, but everybody does. We'll get there … sooner than later. But we did what we came to do."
Each team won four matches that were wrestled. Easton had three pinfalls to St. Michaels' two, and also picked up one more forfeit win than its county rival.

title: Buccaneers fall to Decatur, bounce back against Tech
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Buccaneers fall to Decatur, bounce back against Tech

 February 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1052

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — The streak — which unofficially reached 61 consecutive victories against Bayside Conference opponents Wednesday night — is not the overwhelming driving force.No, what really pushes Stephen Decatur High's wrestling team is the idea it won't be good enough after graduating its state champions and finishers from the previous year.
"The kids know we haven't lost a Bayside match in awhile," Seahawks head coach Josh August said. "But I feel like each year, we have like really good guys, state champs that graduated and go off to college, and then the guys that are left feel like they have something to prove. Because when you have a state champ, or two state champs leave, (people) think that you are not going to be as good. I think our guys use that to motivate themselves, keep on carrying on with the wins and making states."
Decatur kept carrying on Wednesday night, routing non-conference foe Harford Vo-Tech, 61-9, before defeating Kent Island, 44-23, to extend its Bayside dominance while remaining undefeated heading Friday's showdown with unbeaten Rising Sun.
"I thought we wrestled really good against Harford Tech," said August, after the Seahawks improved to 13-0 overall, 10-0 Bayside. "Some of our guys stepped up big, went up a couple weights for the Kent Island match. Not a lot of guys do that. We got guys wanting to wrestle big matches. Overall, I think the team is clicking pretty good."
Overall, Kent Island head coach Tommy Sitar was happy with how his team battled against Decatur, which routed the Buccaneers, 60-18 at the Iron Duals in early January.
"We won only three matches against them," Sitar said of the Iron Horse dual against Decatur. "(Tonight) we won six matches, doubled our output, which is nice."
Perhaps the nicest part of the Decatur match for Kent Island was after losing the first three weight classes to Juan Hinojosa (113), Liam Hugues (120) and Reid Caimi (126) by pin to fall behind 18-0, the Bucs (10-3, 8-1) won the next four weights to pull within 18-14.
"They definitely looked strong," Sitar said of Silas Brobst (132), Greg Couch (138), Cody Sandefer (144) and Ashton Main (150). "I was impressed with the way they were able to dictate to the other wrestlers what was going to happen."
Brobst start the mini-rally when he went into overtime tied 1-1 with Aaron August then scored a takedown with 26 seconds left in the 1-minute overtime for a 3-1 sudden victory.
"Silas wrestled his best match definitely on his feet," Sitar said. "The way he was moving and setting him up was awesome."
Kent Island's next three wrestlers would each score the first takedown in their respective matches. Couch scored a late takedown for a 9-1 major decision over Jake Saullo. Sandefer built a 10-0 lead over two periods en route to a 12-3 major over Alex Riehl. Main capped the run with a 10-3 decision over Braydon Bell at 150.
Despite having its lead trimmed to four, Coach August was pleased with how his team wrestled through the middleweights.
"The score looked closer than the last time we went against Kent Island," Josh August said. "They're a solid team every year. We came away with the victory. It was a little close in the middle, but they are strong right there. One of our things was our guys weren't getting pinned. Our guys that were outmatched were hanging in there, wrestling the full six minutes."
The Seahawks seized full control from there, packaging three pinfalls and two major decisions over the next five bouts for a 44-23 lead.
Decatur's Amarian Manuel earned a 16-8 major over Brandon Adler at 157. Parker Intrieri pinned Chris Kougoures in 47 seconds at 165. Gavin Solito — wrestling up from 157 — put together a 9-1 major over Giuseppe Mellinger at 175. Kole Kohut (190) pinned Brian Potter in 1:49, and Nate McDaniel pinned Nick Morey with 28 seconds remaining in the 215-pound match.
"I think it's an expectation by them," Josh August said of his team's mindset. "It's an expectation that they wrestle to the level to get there, not that they are just going to get there."
Kent Island came back to win the last two bouts, Greg Coffey winning a 4-2 decision over Price Hill at 285, and Gavin Lindner pinning Jaxon Archer in 3:08 at 106.
The 21-point difference was the closest any Bayside team has come to Decatur this season.
The Bucs fell behind 7-0 to Harford Vo Tech, but then regrouped to win 10 of the remaining 12 bouts, which included pinfalls from Couch (138), Adler (157), Kougoures (166), Potter (190), Morey (215), Coffey (285) and Lindner (106).
"I talked to the guys after the Decatur match 'cause it appeared we started at a weight (120) where had kind of a letdown," Sitar said. "I let them know, 'We're peaking. We haven't peaked. Decatur was not the peak. We don't stop now just because we wrestled a team tough. We keep on peaking."
Wedged in the Bucs' rally was Sitar's decision to insert Potter, a 175-pound backup, in at 190 and bump Morey from 190 to 215.
"At the end of the match we had a situation where we were going to be (potentially) down 15 with five bouts left, or we could be down potentially 15 with three bouts left," Sitar said. "So I opted with the strategy of going down 15 with three bouts, and bumped our 190 (Morey) to 215, where I was 100 percent sure he could get a pinfall. And our backup 175-pounder, Brian Potter ended up getting a pin over Jack Ryder of Harford Tech, who I guess was ranked in the state."
Brobst won a 13-3 major decision at 132 and Sandefer got a 7-3 decision at 144 to help the Bucs take a 13-7 lead. Tech's Ryan Sewell pinned Main at 150 to tie the match at 13-all before Kent Island won the next seven straight matches, which included a 6-2 decision by Mellinger at 175.
"It's nice to immediately erase it from the forefront," Sitar said of coming back and beating Harford Tech after the Decatur loss.
Notes: Kent Island's three losses this season have come against Decatur, which is bidding for a fifth consecutive state dual-meet title — excluding the COVID-19 canceled 2021 season — two-time defending 1A state dual-meet champ and unbeaten South Carroll, and Class 4A Broadneck (9-3).

title: HOME RULE
author: Bill Haufe
content:
HOME RULE

 February 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Home Rule 
 
 1088

 Read News Document

 BERLIN — Now that a fifth consecutive state dual-meet championship has been tucked away, Stephen Decatur High head wrestling coach Josh August said his team can focus on individual competition at the regional and state levels, though the approach is slightly different."There are certain things that you would do," August said, comparing dual-meet to individual competition. "If you're losing, you don't give up the bonus, or you don't get pinned in a dual meet because that score matters. But out here, like if you're down, sometimes you got to let it fly. You might not get the takedown but you went for it. The mentality is a little different, but overall just go out, wrestle tough, get to the positions you prefer. Most of the time things work out pretty good for you."
Things again worked out pretty good for the Seahawks Monday, as they placed nine in the finals and left with seven individual titles on the way to winning their fifth straight Bayside Conference championship in their home gym.
Decatur totaled 269½ points to easily outdistance runner-up Parkside by 86½ points. Kent Island was third with 179½ points, followed by North Caroline (fourth, 166), Colonel Richardson (fifth, 146½) and Queen Anne's County (sixth, 123).
"They are just a really tight team," August said. "The momentum from state duals definitely kind of bleeds over into this."
Decatur reached the finals in the first five weight classes, with Juan Hinojosa (33-3) leading off with a fall over Kent Island freshman Gavin Lindner (27-10) in 1 minute, 47 seconds in the 106-pound title match. Elijah Collick (35-2) followed with a 16-4 major decision over Queen Anne's freshman Alan McDonald (30-7) in the 113 final. Liam Hugues (14-5) made it three straight titles for the Seahawks with a 7-1 decision over Wicomico's Tavenon Outlaw (29-7) at 120.
Decatur's Reid Caimi (32-2) advanced to the 126-pound final but forfeited to Queen Anne's senior Tremaine Jackson (32-3) due to injury.
The Seahawks' win streak ended at 132, where Kent Island's Greg Couch (27-7) scored takedowns in each period for a 7-0 victory over Decatur's Aaron August (29-5).
"He's been wrestling 38 for most of this year," Kent Island head coach Tommy Sitar said of Couch. "He came down and had a great day."
Amarian Manuel (34-8) gave Decatur its fourth individual crown with a 9-2 decision over Parkside's Xavier Moorman (19-3) at 150. Teammate Gavin Solito (39-1) built a 7-1 lead before pinning Kent Island's Brandon Adler (22-12) in the 157-pound final. Senior Parker Intrieri (28-2) completed the Seahawks' second three-match win streak of the finals, earning a 14-1 major decision over Colonel Richardson sophomore Derrick Mitchell (32-7) at 165.
Two bouts later, Decatur senior Kole Kohut (32-6) pieced together a 12-4 major decision over Kent Island's Nick Morey (32-5) to win the 190-pound weight class.
The only other teams with multiple winners were Kent Island and Parkside.
The Bucs got their second crown from senior Giuseppe Mellinger (33-5), who after surrendering an escape to Parkside's Canaan Mapp (22-7), strung together a second-period takedown, with an escape and another takedown in the third period en route to a 7-2 decision at 175.
"Giuseppe, another awesome tournament," said Sitar, who had six in the finals, including Cody Sandefer (29-9), the runner-up at 144. "We were kind of hoping we'd get seven in there today, but I'm pretty happy with the effort. Those guys that didn't make it for the most part wrestled back pretty well. I'm proud of our team score."
Parkside got pinfalls from Shaheed Armstrong (33-6) and Ali'i Turner (24-5) to win the 215- and 285-pound titles, respectively, and nudge past Kent Island for second place in the team standings.
Kent County sophomore Scottie Ford (34-1) was the fourth wrestler from a North Bayside school to win a title, as he crafted a 6-0 decision over Parkside's Rocco Tully (33-8) to win the 138-pound weight class.
North Caroline's fourth-place finish was bolstered by eight top-four finishes, including four winners in the consolation finals — Darly Ortega (106), Edward Darling (157), Tommy Morris (215) and Daketa Kinsey (285).
Sophomore Chatydrick Pickrom (23-13) gave Colonel Richardson a second finalist in the boys' competition as he reached the 285-pound final, where he lost to Turner.
"I would say it's definitely up there," Colonel Richardson head coach Bryan Hall said of the Colonel's fifth-place finish possibly being its best in conference tournament history for his program. "They did very well. We only had one guy that didn't place in the top seven."
The Colonels also finished with four champions in the girls division. Dale Swann (16-7) pinned Decatur's Melanie Ruiz (5-8) in 1:16 to win the 105-pound crown. Freshman Olivia McGregor (15-1) pinned Queen Anne's Lilly Hammond (14-5) in 3:26 to win the 145-pound division. Teammate Hannah Kefauver (9-7) almost duplicated that effort, pinning Decatur's Amari Purnell (9-4) in 3:25 of the 155-pound final.
"They wrestled well," Hall said of his girls. "We kind of expected Olivia McGregor to win. She only lost one match on the season. The finals match she wrestled very tough. She was down early and was able to come back and pin the girl.
"Hannah, she really showed up," Hall continued. "She showed a lot of grit, wrestled hard, beat two tough girls. And Dale of course, I think she beat everyone in the weight class, so she beat them all again."
Ryleigh Porter (7-3) was Colonel's fourth champ, but the only other wrestler in the 235-pound weight class dropped out of the tournament. Colonel's Luna Infante-Reyes (110), Landine Dorleans (125) and Danika Jeanty (170) each placed second.
Lilliana Mellinger (8-1) gave Kent Island its lone girls champion when she earned a 10-5 victory over Queen Anne's Ava Price (15-6) in the 120-pound final.
Queen Anne's finished with three conference champions, including Ally Conley (17-5) — the 2022 2A-1A state champion — who pinned Parkside's Logan Newton (7-4) in 30 seconds to win the 100-pound title.
The Lions' other two finals wins came against teammates. Keira Corcoran (4-3) earned a 3-2 decision over Linda Vail (7-9) to win the 135-pound weight class, and Julia Reburn (12-6) pinned Emma Coppage (2-8) in the 140-pound final.
"Overall I would say it was a great day for girls wrestling in the Bayside, finally getting the tournament going," said Queen Anne's boys head coach David Stricker, who has played a key role in the growth of girls wrestling in the state. "Team-wise we did pretty well. I think we kind of underachieved a little bit. We had a rough semifinals and finals. It was sort of a reality check for some of our girls going into regionals Friday."

PLACING THEMSELVES

 February 24, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Last Monday's Bayside Conference championships was not one of the more memorable performances by Queen Anne's County High's young girls wrestling program."We didn't wrestle our best," Lions head coach John Waters said.
But Waters used Monday as a learning tool heading into Friday's Class 2A-1A East Regional championships.
"I think with a lot of young wrestlers, not knowing what Baysides mean, Monday was probably the best thing for us because it showed that the girls needed to be focused and ready for every match. A few of them at Baysides won their first match and they weren't ready for the semifinals."
The Lions certainly appeared ready Friday, placing in 11 of the 14 weight classes for a group that now advances to the Class 2A-1A state championships, beginning Thursday at the Show Place Arena in Upper Marlboro.
The top three finishers in each weight class in the four regional girls tournaments advance, where the boys tournaments advance the top four at each weight.
"Overall I'm proud of the girls," said Waters, who had 10 in the championship finals and left with four individual champs. "They really wrestled well. They've worked extremely hard to get where they are. Most of the girls on the team are first-year wrestlers. And if they're not first, they're second. So that says a lot about where they've come. Most of the varsity lineup are freshmen and sophomores."
Among that group, freshman Finley Patchett (125 pounds) and sophomore Bree Conard (115) each managed to win titles after being turned to their backs, as did junior Ally Conley (100).
"That just says a lot about their focus at practice this week," Waters said.
Conley (17-5) scored an early takedown against Parkside's Logan Newton (7-5), got turned, but recovered to earn a pin in 1 minute, 20 seconds to win the 100-pound crown. Conard (14-7) battled off her back and built a 10-4 lead before pinning Parkside's Brylee Davis (15-7) in 4:29 of the 115-pound final.
Then there was Patchett (13-4), who led 7-1 after one period against Stephen Decatur's Rachel Plata (9-2) in the 125-pound final. Patchett was leading 9-2 when Plata escaped, scored a takedown and picked up three near-fall points to close within 9-8 heading into the third. But Patchett, starting off bottom, hit a reversal 17 seconds into the third and added a late takedown for a 13-9 decision.
Junior Keira Corcoran (4-3) gave Queen Anne's a fourth champion when she pinned Decatur's Aya Mejber (2-11) in 3:45 to win the 135-pound championship. Corcoran got a takedown one minute into the match, but Mejber escaped to make it 2-1 entering the second period. Corcoran worked an escape 32 seconds into the second and got a takedown before earning her fall.
"We talked at practice about just being ready, staying focused," Waters said. "And doing what they're best at; not trying to do something they saw on Youtube or something. Just do what you're good at."
Queen Anne's got runner-up finishes from Ava Price (15-6) at 120, Delaney Gray (15-7) at 130, Julia Reburn (11-7) at 140, Lilly Hammond (14-5) at 145, Morgan Morris (5-6) at 170, and Kaylynn Bryant (17-4) at 190. Maggie Rooney (3-7) placed third at 235.
"There were a few matches, especially in the finals, we just came out a little flat," Waters said. "It's hard to come back unless you're ready. But the ones that lost in the finals, they'll have a couple good days of practice, they'll bounce back. They'll be ready. They'll refocus. That's what we're looking for."
Colonel Richardson will have the East's second largest contingent at states, as it qualified eight, led by junior Ryleigh Porter (9-3), who pinned Cambridge-South Dorchester's Sienna Mitchell (9-7) to win the 235-pound weight class.
Colonel's Dale Swann (17-8) lost by fall in the 105-pound final, but four teammates earned pins in the consolation finals.
Luna Infante-Reyes (11-13) pinned Kent County's Rhilynne Ashley-Pinder (4-11) in 4:44 of the 110-pound final. Frankie Aguiar (5-8) earned a 59-second fall over Decatur's Jessica Garcia (1-10) for third place at 120. Landine Dorleans (14-12) defeated James M. Bennett's Sinai Horsey (12-23) via a 2:35 pin at 125. And Olivia McGregor (17-2) wrestled back to earn a 3:46 fall over Queen Anne's Adelina Dickens (8-16) at 1:55.
Colonel's Annabelle Morales (2-11) and Danika Jeanty (4-9) won their consolation finals at 130 and 170, respectively with a bye.
Kent Island went two for two in the championship finals.
Sophomore Lilliana Mellinger (10-1) got a pair of takedowns before pinning Queen Anne's Price in 1:25 to win the 120-pound title. And senior Kendra Coffey (6-2) bundled two first-period takedowns with a second-period escape en route to a 5-2 decision over Queen Anne's Hammond in the 145-pound final.

author: Bill Haufe
content:
TIME TRIALS

 February 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1299
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Giuseppe Mellinger needed a late block.Tremaine Jackson needed an extra minute.
And Scottie Ford. Well, he needed more time than either one of them.
No matter the time frame, Jackson, Ford and Mellinger each finished with the same result Saturday night at Queen Anne's County High, winning their respective weight classes at the Class 2A-1A East Regional wrestling championships.
"He's been one of our elite wrestlers for three years now," Queen Anne's head coach David Stricker said of Jackson, who with his 5-3 overtime victory against Rising Sun's Xzavier Brown in the 126-pound final earned his 99th career win. "Tremaine, he's just so quick. And his power has really come along this year. When he gets in on a leg it's really hard to fend off."
Saturday's region final was the third time Jackson and Brown faced off this season. Brown pieced together an 8-3 decision at the Westminster Duals in late December, then earned a 3-1 overtime win when the two met in the 2A-1A East Regional Duals earlier this month. Their third encounter would also take longer than six minutes.
"They've been wrestling each other since youth, so they've known each other really well," Stricker said. "I'm not surprised it went that far."
A senior, Jackson (35-3) scored a first-period takedown, but Brown escaped with 44 seconds left in the period to make it 2-1 after one. Brown (35-8) rode Jackson through a scoreless second period, and hit a reversal 11 seconds into the third period for a 3-2 lead. Jackson then got an escape off a restart with 15 seconds left in the third to forge a 3-3 tie, sending the match into a 1-minute overtime.
"It's obviously been a bit harder because they've been training him, trying to study my style, his coaches," Jackson said. "They obviously know me very well, the good moves I do. So yeah, it definitely was a lot more difficult than the other times wrestling him."
Brown got in a single-leg shot in the overtime, but Jackson blocked, spun and earned the takedown for the 5-3 sudden victory.
"My last match at the high school, and what was going through my head was, I can't lose," said Jackson, whose second regional title came five days after winning his third Bayside Conference crown. "I feel great. I put in the work. I think I've got a good shot of getting in the state finals."
Ford also had a familiar opponent in his 138-pound final — Parkside junior Rocco Tully — who the Kent County sophomore decisioned 6-0 in the Bayside championship five days earlier.
"I knew it was going to be tougher," said Ford, who coupled two takedowns with a reversal for Monday's 6-0 victory. "Every time you wrestle somebody it feels like it gets tougher and tougher. They always learn from it. I was nervous. I would have much rather faced somebody else I hadn't seen before."
After a scoreless first period, Ford (37-1) hit a switch off bottom for a reversal with 35 seconds left in the second period for a 2-0 lead. Tully (35-9) scored a takedown with 44 seconds to go in the third and rode Ford the rest of the period, forcing overtime.
Neither wrestler scored in the 1-minute overtime. Starting on top, Ford rode Tully through the first 30-second sudden-victory period. Less than two seconds into the second 30-second period, Ford reversed Tully and rode out the remainder of the period on top for the 4-2 win.
"I knew I had a good switch on him because on Monday I had a nice switch," Ford said. "He knows how to throw legs, so he's really tough on top, but I knew I could get out. I just beat him off the whistle."
Something that did not surprise Kent County head coach Chris Yiannakis.
"He's been on that switch," Yiannakis said of Ford. "That's one of his number one escapes from bottom. Most people can't stop it. It's so fast. Rocco did stop it in the first couple of periods though. He just wore him down by the final (period) and he couldn't stop it."
The 175-pound final was yet another Bayside rematch, as Mellinger (36-5) clashed with Parkside's Canaan Mapp (24-8) for the third time this season.
"The first time we wrestled he actually was more aggressive," said Mellinger, who defeated Mapp via a 12-4 major decision during the dual-meet season. "He would actually tie up with me and stuff. So that allowed me to work my offense. The second time, at Baysides (a 7-2 Mellinger win), he would run around, he kept moving, but I got a few takedowns there.
"This time, because I think his coaches were telling him how to make some good adjustments, he wasn't tying up," Mellinger continued. "He was keeping me at a distance. He would try to work in some shots, I would try to work in mine. But we both got a good shot defense. And then when we're so far apart, it's hard to score points."
Mellinger got a double-leg takedown 54 seconds into the match, but Mapp escaped 11 seconds later, making it 2-1 heading into the second. Mapp escaped five seconds into he second period to tie the match.
It remained that way until 18 seconds into the third, when Mellinger, starting on bottom, escaped to take a 3-2 lead. Mellinger blocked a shot midway through the period before a neutral restart with 41 seconds left. Mellinger got in a shot, but Mapp countered with a shot with less than 20 seconds left. The Kent Island senior, who was named the Bayside Conference's defensive player of the year in football for 2023, could not be taken down though, hanging on for the 3-2 win.
"I started getting a little nervous at the end when I took a shot and then he re-shot and got in on my leg with like 15 seconds left," Mellinger said. "And I was able to defend that because if he had gotten that and I didn't get up in time, that would have been the match."
It was Mellinger's first regional title.
"It's nice to win, said Mellinger, whose younger sister Lilliana won the 120-pound title at Friday night's girls 2A-1A East Regional. "My sister and I, we're both Bayside champions. Now, we're both regional champions. Now, we're both competing for a state title. That's cool. It's a lot of fun."
Said Kent Island head coach Tommy Sitar of Mellinger, "He had another great tournament. He worked really well in his matches leading up to the final, and fortunately got the win in the final. It's hard to beat a wrestler three times in a season. It's a good feat."
Kent Island seniors Greg Couch (132) and Cody Sandefer (144) each took runner-up honors, and seniors Brandon Adler (157) and Nick Morey (190) each won their consolation final to place third.
The top four in each weight class advance to this year's state tournament, which begins Thursday at the Show Place Arena in Upper Marlboro and concludes Saturday.
Stephen Decatur and Rising Sun each advanced nine to states, while North Caroline finished with the most wrestlers from a North Bayside school, qualifying six and two alternates.
"We had a rough Monday at Baysides," North Caroline head coach Robin Eaton said. "I preached to them all week 'That wasn't the week to shine. 'Work harder and fix a few things and we could shine at regionals.' And that's what they did. They did everything we worked on; wrestled very smart, wrestled tough. Didn't make mistakes."
North Caroline freshman Caleb Melvin (120), junior Corey Bunce (165) and senior Dakota Kinsey (285) each wrestled-back to win their respective consolation finals, while sophomores Darly Ortega (106), Connor Frank (113), and Jacob Carpenter (126) placed fourth.
Kent County senior Brady Sutton decisioned Harford Vo Tech's Nikolai Chervak in the 144-pound consolation final, and Cambridge-South Dorchester sophomore Mark Jones placed fourth at 285.

title: STATE CHAMPS
author: Bill Haufe
content:
STATE CHAMPS

 March 6, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1457
 Words 

 Read News Document

 David Stricker was trying to digest the past three days.Or maybe it was the past three years.
Some 16 hours earlier, Queen Anne's County High's girls wrestling team and coaching staff piled onto a podium at the Show Place Arena in Upper Marlboro in celebration of winning the first-ever team title at the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association's girls state wrestling tournament.
Seated at the end of a long table inside a school conference room early Sunday afternoon, Stricker was still wrestling to find the right words as he looked at the state championship trophy perched in front of him.
"As I told the girls, I had about three sentences of a speech prepared in my brain and I only got to about three, and then I started rambling," Stricker said with a smile. "It's just humbling. Even this morning, flipping through pictures and stuff, I still tear up just thinking about it."
It's only been three years since Stricker, Queen Anne's boys head wrestling coach, started the school's girls program.
That first team had only three girls but ended the season with then-freshman Ally Conley winning the 100-pound state title.
The program grew to 14 last season, and 22 this season, which started with a December bus ride to the Maverick Duals at Manchester Valley, during which Stricker and girls head coach John Waters joked about possibly winning a state title.
The Lions went 11-0 in dual-meet competition, which included defeating Winters Mill in the first dual meet in MPSSAA history where both teams filled all 14 weight classes.
They had three individual champions at the Bayside Conference tournament. Four days later, they crowned four champions at the Class 2A-1A East Region championships.
Then came the newly formatted three-day state tournament, which ended Saturday night with Conley earning a second-period pin in the 100-pound final for her second state title in three years.
"Yes, we ended up with that," Waters said Sunday, nodding toward the state championship trophy. "We earned that. But we wanted the girls and the entire team, coaches included, to enjoy the moment. We told them Thursday when we get there, 'Take pictures. Walk around the building. No matter what, us coaches will be there next year hopefully. But we're not going to bring the same team back. This team was special.'"
Queen Anne's had a wrestler in 12 of the 14 weight classes at states. Of those 12, only one, Morgan Morris, didn't win a match.
But Morris was symbolic of the hard work ethic Waters, Stricker and assistant Jimmy Swindell forever preached at practice.
Morris lost in a wrestle-off at 155 pounds with teammate Adelina Dickens prior to the conference championships. The sophomore could easily have opted to begin focusing on the upcoming softball season. Instead, Waters and Stricker asked if Morris would consider bumping up to 170 for regionals.
"We don't have anybody there," Waters said to Morris of the weight class, "and there's a good chance you might make states."
Though there were only three wrestlers in the 170 bracket at regionals, Morris chose to give it a shot, won a match, and placed second to qualify for states.
"She did one heckuva job," Waters said of Morris, who wrestled opponents that not only had 15 to 20 pounds on her, but had more experience. "She came across a couple of tough matches. The girls were just heavier."
Queen Anne's other 11 wrestlers won at least once.
Senior Julia Reburn, one of the originals on the inaugural 2021-22 team, earned a win at 140, as did sophomores Lilly Hammond (145), Dickens (155) and Maggie Rooney (220).
Juniors Ava Price (120) and Keira Corcoran (135) each went 2-2. Senior Delaney Gray (130), another 2022 original, went 3-2 and reached the consolation quarterfinals, as did sophomore Bree Conard, who went 2-2 at 115.
And while Conley went 4-0 en route to the title that capped a 21-5 season, no Lions wrestler won more over the tournament's three days than Kaylynn Bryant.
Bryant won her pigtail match at 190, lost 5-4 to two-time defending state champion Jabea Ewane of Winters Mill, then never lost again.
The junior pinned her first two consolation-bracket opponents, then gutted out a 5-4 victory in an ultimate tiebreaker. She earned another one-point decision in the quarterfinals, then pinned her next two opponents, notching a 4:33 fall in the consolation final.
"I knew she could get on the podium. But she just kept going," said Stricker of Bryant, who went 7-1 to finish a 24-5 season. "Actually her pin in the consolation quarterfinals is what kind of put us over the top team score wise."
Then there was Finley Patchett at 125.
"Finley and Kaylynn, they surpassed what they were supposed to do," Waters said. "Kaylynn we kind of figured she'd come back to get in that third- and fourth-(place) match.
"But Finley was a wild card because she's only wrestled for two months," Waters continued. "And she was probably in the hardest weight class from top to bottom. And she's one of the few freshmen in that weight class. A lot of the other girls were 11th graders with four or five years of wrestling experience."
Patchett (17-6) wrestled nothing but juniors the whole tournament. She won by fall in the first round before getting pinned in her second match. After winning her first two consolation bouts by decision, she lost by fall in the consolation semifinals, but bounced back with a pin to place fifth.
"Finley as a first-year wrestler just did amazing things," Stricker said. "At the beginning of the season she was in sort of a logjam with Bree and Ava. We were trying to figure out what weight class to get her to go to. As the season went on we kind of got everybody situated, and once she got more consistent mat time, I mean she just really kind of started to take off."
"She did extra practice at home," Stricker added. "Then what she did at the state tournament. … That's the biggest state tournament that there's ever been. There were 24 girls per weight class, which was even more than the boys (16 per weight class). The depth and the ability in the tournament, and then for her to go out and take fifth, and only lose to people who finished above her on the podium" — Hammond junior Clara Freeman (third, 21-13) and Montgomery Blair junior Joni Chuka (fourth, 24-7) — "was really impressive."
As has Queen Anne's rapid rise to the top.
"There's a joke in my house," Stricker said. "My wife says, 'My son can swim, but my daughters can wrestle.' So when I started this, my whole thought, at least at our school, was to take away the stigma of girls wrestling. It's not like this novelty thing, that one girl wrestler on the team."
Other schools around the state began building strong girls programs, most notably Manchester Valley, Francis Scott Key, Winters Mill, La Plata and Eastern Tech. Waters began tracking those "so-called big dogs" in tournaments and noticed a trend.
"I remember all the big-dog schools, they're just talking about these certain schools," Waters said. "I remember going to Dave and saying, 'There's a lot of good girls out there wrestling right now that these schools. ... they're not giving them any credit. These girls are going to come in and there's not going to be one team that dominates and wins like six state girls titles this year. It's going to be a lot of random schools with three or four good girls.'"
Waters was proven correct at states, with no school having more than one champion in the 14 weight classes.
Queen Anne's girls head coach also thought the way his team wrestled, it could challenge for a state title in the near future.
"We had four first-year wrestlers go to states," Waters said. "And we have some girls with only two years experience. So I'm thinking by Ally's senior year they should be able to push for the team title."
That time frame got pushed up last weekend, as the Lions amassed 119 points on the way to the title, outdistancing runner-up Oakland Mills (86), third-place Francis Scott Key (82) and fourth-place Stephen Decatur and Eastern Tech (80).
Fifteen of Queen Anne's combined 21 losses at the tournament came against wrestlers who placed in the top six.
"It's like they are on the forefront of the state of Maryland in the fastest growing sport in the nation," Stricker said. "They're doing more than I ever could have possibly imagined.
"I figured it would take us 10, 15 years to get to this point," Stricker said with another head nod toward the state trophy. "And I mean we led it from Thursday to Saturday the whole time. We were always in first."

author: Bill Haufe
content:
CLOSING STATEMENTS

 March 21, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1379

 Read News Document

 UPPER MARLBORO — Giuseppe Mellinger didn't storm past his coaches, chuck his headgear in a fury, or try to leave an impression on the nearest concrete wall with his fist.The opportunity to direct blame was certainly there, but the Kent Island High senior refused to point a finger.
"I'm not going to make excuses for myself," Mellinger said in the wake of a 3-2 ultimate-tiebreaker loss in the 175-pound final during the Class 2A/1A state wrestling championship tournament at the Show Place Arena on March 2. "You try not to let refs dictate your match. Wrestling you know, you've got to be accountable. It's only you out there wrestling somebody else."
Of the 16 wrestlers from North Bayside schools that qualified for states, Mellinger was the only one to reach the finals in the boys competition.
"Coming from Kent Island, we rarely have people that make it that far," said Mellinger, who became just the third Buccaneer to reach the finals during Tommy Sitar's eight seasons as head coach — joining Matt Miller (2020) and Justin Thomas (2016). "So it was surreal to be there in that moment.
"Senior year. You've wrestled three years of high school," Mellinger added. "Wrestled since you were like five or six years old, and then you make it to the state finals. Like wow. This is it. But I felt pretty confident. I felt relaxed. That was my last match ever so I'm going to go out there and let it fly. Like it's just one more match."
On the way to that last match, Mellinger had earned a first-round 15-13 win over Hammond's Jaden Timithy in the first sudden-victory period, took a forfeit in the quarterfinals, then defeated Middletown senior Kashton Dalhouse (47-4) via a 5-4 decision in the semifinals.
That set up his title shot with South Carroll sophomore Anthony Rodrigues (47-3). With 45 seconds remaining in the first period, the lead official held up two fingers, signaling a two-point takedown for Mellinger. But that initial call was waved off when the official ruled Mellinger did not to have enough control.
"I thought I did too," said Mellinger when asked if he thought he had the takedown. "I didn't hear anybody argue against it. And the South Carroll guys, their body language was like, 'Yeah, wow. We got saved on that one.'"
Though he did not protest or go to the scorer's table for an explanation, Sitar also thought Mellinger had a takedown.
"I would have liked to see that call stand at two," Sitar said. "It wasn't something where they came to the table an overturned it or anything like that, or even that the second ref came in and overturned it."
It remained scoreless through the remainder of the first. Starting on bottom, Rodrigues scored an escape just two seconds into the second period for a 1-0 lead. Sixteen seconds into the third, Mellinger escaped off bottom, to make it 1-1. Mellinger blocked a shot 14 seconds later and after two restarts, the score remained 1-1 heading into overtime.
Mellinger got two deep shots in during the 1-minute overtime, but Rodrigues wouldn't be taken down as the duel moved into the two 30-second ride-out periods. Rodrigues again escaped with only two seconds elapsed for a 2-1 lead. Mellinger answered with an escape with six seconds left in the second ride-out, forging a 2-2 deadlock heading into the ultimate tiebreaker.
Because he had scored the match's first point, Rodrigues got to choose top or bottom to start the final period. Rodrigues took bottom and six seconds into the final stage pulled his left leg from Mellinger's grasp for a 3-2 victory.
"That (takedown) would have won the championship," said Sitar (39-6), who was bidding to become Kent Island's first state champion since 2015 when Stevan Smith won his second straight state title. "Whoever had a takedown was going to win because shots were so hard.
"I was hoping for a state title," Mellinger added. "But at the end of the day I was the aggressive wrestler. As the match went on, offense got harder and harder, especially when we got sweaty. Nothing you can down now."
Kent Island senior Greg Couch (132 pounds) had his hopes for a state championship end in Friday's semifinal round, when he lost a 12-6 decision to defending — and eventual — state champion JoJo Gigliotti of South Carroll.
"I think he gave him his toughest match," Sitar said of Couch's battle with Gigliotti. "I think he knew he had a match with Couch. I think had Couch been on the other side of the bracket I might have had a couple of finalists. Greg wrestled his butt off. He was peaking at the right time."
Couch looked headed for the consolation bracket, when he fell behind 4-0 in the first period of his opening match to Southern Garrett's Hayden Harvey.
"He got taken down twice and then it was like the switch was flipped," Sitar said of Couch. "He was ready to go. He was comfortable and he just let the rest of the weight class have it from there."
Starting with Harvey, who would not score another point while Couch was rallying for a 13-4 major decision. Couch earned a 7-1 decision over Huntingtown senior Jett Cramer (24-5) in the quarterfinals but then lost 12-6 to Gigliotti (51-1), who pinned his other three opponents in the tournament en route to his second state title.
"When I got into the consi round I realized, 'This is all or nothing,'" Couch said. "'This is my senior year. This is all I got left.'"
And it took some doing.
Couch and C. Milton Wright's Mitchell Nguyen (36-8) were tied 2-2 through regulation and overtime. Couch then rode Nguyen out through the first ride-out stage before working an escape in the second ride-out for a 3-2 win.
"That was definitely one of my hardest matches of the year, it not the hardest," Couch said of his bout with Nguyen.
In the consolation final, Couch crafted a 7-2 victory over Northern Garrett's Mason Glotfelty (39-5) for his 100th career victory and a third-place finish.
"I had a lot going through my mind before that last match," said Couch, who finished 33-9. "I had the support of my family. My dad and my uncle were on the mat coaching for me in my corner. It definitely provided me with everything I needed for that last match.
"It was definitely a hard path back to try to get third," Couch said. "They say second place usually looks the most upset and third is smiling a lot more, and I can definitely agree with that. Definitely makes a difference ending it on a win rather than a loss."
Queen Anne's County senior Tremaine Jackson earned his 100th career win when he earned a 54-second fall in his first-round match on Thursday, but watched his state-title aspirations end Friday with a 4-2 loss to Northern Garrett's Devon Opel (38-7) in the 126-pound quarterfinals.
"I had the whole night (Friday) to think about what happened," Jackson said of his loss. "I mean it hurt, but I knew I just had to bounce back, just start doing what I do best."
Jackson's road to the consolation final started Saturday morning with a 15-0 technical fall over Liberty's Alex Pearl in 3:15. He advanced to the consolation semifinals with a forfeit, then put together a 13-0 major decision over Eastern Vo Tech's Chase Ullman."
"The tech fall, the (Pearl) kid walked off the mat and he was like, 'Man, that kid is fricking good,' when he shook my hand," Queen Anne's head coach David Stricker said. "We were like, 'Yeah, we know.'
"He could just stop putting the pressure on himself and just go be Tremaine, and pretty much show off his full talents; his full arsenal," Stricker said of Jackson after his quarterfinal loss. "When he's there and he can just let it fly, there's not a whole lot of people that can stop him."
That included Rising Sun's Xzavier Brown, who faced off for a fourth time this season against Jackson in the consolation final and lost 5-2.
"It was close but I feel like I calculated that match," said Jackson, whose second consecutive third-place finish at states capped a 40-4 season. "I wrestled him a bunch of times. And that was my last high school match, so I was coming out on top regardless."

Girls wrestling champions receive acclamation

 June 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Making history as the first girls wrestling team to win the Maryland State Championship during the 2023-2024 season, the Liberty Building packed with supporters as Queen Anne's County High School Lions received official recognition and forever acclamation from county commissioners and state delegates May 28.Delegate Jay Jacobs (R-36) presented a Maryland General State Assembly official citation to recognize the historic achievement along with the county commissioners congratulating the Lions on winning the Maryland Secondary School Sports Athletic Association Girls Wrestling State Championship.
Coach David Stricker was immensely proud of the continual strong teamwork demonstrated by the Lions and the recognition that validated all their hard work.
Since its inception, the team has blossomed to over 20 members and the Lions have never stopped giving it their all, Coach Stricker said.
Team Captain and graduating senior Julia Reburn was one of three original members when the team got started her freshman year.
"I can't put into words what this means. It feels well deserved for the whole team," Reburn said.
The team have always supported each other and have pushed each other physically and mentally to be the best they could be.
"We've certainly paid our dues," she said.
Reburn considered joining the wrestling team, "the best decision I ever made" and highly encouraged students with an interest in wrestling, especially girls, to check out the sport.
"It's a girl's sport just as much as a boys," she said.

Wicomico defeats Easton

 December 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — Jason Biringer has no illusion of flipping Easton High's wrestling program around overnight."It's growing pains," said Biringer, who has returned as the Warriors head coach after three seasons away from the program. "We set small goals for each of these guys. Hey, sometimes it might be just, get through the first period for those super raw new guys. After that we just keep building a little more. Make it through your first match. Get your first win. Get another win. Small steps."
Biringer saw some of his green roster take some small steps Wednesday night during a 58-24 loss to Wicomico, which won four of the five varsity matches wrestled to go along with six forfeit wins.
"We know we have to work," said Biringer, whose roster of 30 has only six wrestlers with more experience than just this season. "And we know there's a lot to do, and a lot of ways to get better. But I'm happy with the effort they are putting in. Like I said, it's a lot to ask."
Wicomico had an 18-6 lead via three forfeits through the first four weight classes, then extended that cushion to 24-6, when Deion Finney pinned AJ Matulay in 1 minute, 4 seconds at 132 pounds.
Easton (0-2) picked up its lone win not by way of forfeit at 138, when Shawn Arnold fell into a 3-0 first-period hole, scored a late escape, then pinned Ethan Brewington at 2:39, pulling the Warriors within 24-12.
"Shawn is a scrappy kid," Biringer said. "We've been working with him. He's got a high octane motor. Getting him to be settle down and be more controlled out there, that's our focus. But he has a ton of potential. He's a second-year kid. Bright future for him if he keeps working hard."
The Indians won the other three matches that were wrestled, the tightest being at 144, where Corey Richardson decisioned Easton's Adonis Schmitt, 7-2. Wi-Hi's Adelson Theajeon pinned Anthony Melendez in 2:45 at 175, and Keven Mondestin got a 21-second fall over Matthew Brunner at 285.
"Those guys who wrestled, we're asking a lot of those kids," Biringer said. "Wi-Hi also has experience. They have a good program. (Head coach) Nate Stone's been there for many years now and always has a solid group."
Wicomico's Terry Scott (106), Tavenon Outlaw (120), Davidson Fortunel (126), Rowan Okerblom (157), Cameron Wawrzenak (165) and Jamier Johnson (215) each won by forfeit.
"We've got a core of guys that have several years of experience, but they are all kind of lumped down in like in the lower weights," Stone said. "But we have a bunch of guys we think are going to do really well. Overall I thought our conditioning was pretty good for it being this early (in the season). And we didn't look super sloppy. So fundamentally we did OK."
Easton's other wins came via forfeit from Estaben Velasquez (113), Matthew Bravo (150) and Wahaab Popal (190).
"We're focused on each individual's production," said Biringer, who was also encouraged by his girls winning three of five matches, and his boys winning three of the seven junior-varsity bouts. "Lot of youth. Almost exclusively sophomores and freshmen, and then a few juniors and two seniors.
"And the kids have had a good attitude," Biringer added. "They're trying. They want to learn the moves. They want to get better. It takes showing up and putting in that work every day. It's a sport of experience and you have to have the long view."

title: Colonel tops Easton, evens slate
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Colonel tops Easton, evens slate

 December 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 AMERICAN CORNER — Easton High's wrestling team is rebuilding this season.Colonel Richardson?
Colonels head coach Bryan Hall winces at the idea of a rebuild, preferring to say, "We're filling in."
Colonel filled in quite nicely Wednesday night, scoring the first takedown in eight of the 10 matches wrestled en route to a 58-24 victory over Easton.
"It hurts 'cause we thought last year we had eight sophomore starters, three freshmen starters, and only one senior," Hall said. "But we've lost four of our starters from last year. One transferred to North Caroline. One is injured. Two decided not to come out. We lost some guys we were going to be counting on as part of our season, so we're filling in."
One of those filling in for Colonel, 120-pounder Elisee Pierre-Louis, won by injury default. Pierre-Louis was taking Otto Perez to the mat, when the Easton freshman injured his arm while trying to brace his fall. Perez was taken by ambulance to have the injury treated.
"That was a momentum punch in the gut for the guys," Easton head coach Jason Biringer said of losing Perez.
Easton (0-3) had built an early 12-0 lead on Skye Matthews' forfeit win at 106, and Esteban Velasquez' 1:59 pinfall over Brody Omohundro at 113.
The injury default cut Easton's lead in half, but Colonel (2-2) won the next three matches. Jayquan Wilkins crafted a 17-2 technical fall over John Seymour at 126, pulling Colonel within 12-11. Zy Nichols (132) and Evan Alexander (138) each won by forfeit, pushing the Colonels' lead to 23-12.
The Warriors stopped that streak when Adonis Schmidt pinned Trynton Parks in 59 seconds of the 144-pound match, drawing the visitors within 23-18.
But Colonel Richardson won six of the final seven matches, scoring bonus points in five of the bouts.
Anthony Alexander (150) started Colonel's roll, pinning Matthew Bravo just as the first-period buzzer sounded. Gary Koeneman (157) followed, working a 19-4 technical fall over Vlad Oslam. Colonel's Ethan Thomas then got turned to his back, yet rolled through on the way to a 2:47 pinfall over Darren Foxwell at 165, stretching the Colonel lead to 40-18.
"They wrestled amazing," Hall said of his team. "We've been shocked by Ethan Thomas. He's a freshman, just started wrestling last year in a middle school club. He's wrestling up a weight class and has been huge.
"Other guys we expected to win, won," Hall continued. "Other guys we're expecting to go out there and wrestle hard, are. It's been a good season so far."
Tony Melendez got Easton back in the win column with a 1:07 fall over freshman Brox Meissner at 175. But the Colonels closed the match, with Richard Taylor (190) pinning Wahaab Popal in 2:15, Wilson Clough (215) winning by forfeit, and Chatydrick Pickrom (285) pinning Matthew Brunner in 2:45.
Still, Biringer was encouraged by what he saw.
"We are seeing some better habits," Biringer said. "We're also seeing some self-destructive moves, where it's, 'Don't make up your own moves. Do the moves you're taught.' Usually when something bad was happening they were trying something that wasn't a fundamental move. So it's beginner's mistakes, but at the same time a lot more effort, and progress is being made."
Colonel's girls earned 39-22 victory in what was Easton's first girls dual meet. Each team won two of the four matches wrestled.
Colonel's Luna Infante-Reyes (115) pinned Leah Gonzalez-Reyes in 3:38, and Estelle Lima (190) earned a 7-0 decision over Khadija Popal.
Easton's wins came from Shiza Gondal (135), who pinned Lizzy Hesson, and Thanh Mai Pham (140), who earned a 10-2 major decision over Aiyanna Groce.
